processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: System modified to synthesize five different alloys in one operation for each alloy system; five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace and were successively filled from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 10×50×130 mm³ blocks rolled to 2±0.1 mm thick, ~500 mm long sheets

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: After reheating and water quenching, the sheets were cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into nine segments of 2×60×55 mm³ per alloy composition.
This is the defining heat treatment for this sample (550 °C / 24 h), after homogenization.
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized austenitic microstructure with increasing α-ferrite content as Al content increases (2–11 wt.%); XRD screening indicates that increasing ferrite content is more relevant to the mechanical-property trend than the presence of κ-carbides or ε-martensite. No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations; some retained Mn microsegregations.

phases_present.volume_fraction: matrix phase; its fraction decreases as Al content increases because ferrite content increases (2–11 wt.% Al)
increases with Al content in the range 2–11 wt.% Al
possibly minor; less relevant than ferrite content for the mechanical trend
possibly minor; less relevant than ferrite content for the mechanical trend

precipitates.distribution: presence considered less relevant than ferrite content for the mechanical trend in this alloy class

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: tensile specimens prepared from 2×60×55 mm³ segments by package spark erosion
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: all values plotted represent averages of three measurements for every material state

yield_strength.value: increases with Al content in the range 2–11 wt.% Al

ultimate_tensile_strength.value: increases with Al content in the range 2–11 wt.% Al

elongation.value: drops as a function of Al content in the range 2–11 wt.% Al

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: XRD analysis performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: phase screening to identify γ austenite, ε martensite, α ferrite, and κ carbide
characterization_methods.key_findings: increasing ferrite content with Al is more relevant to the mechanical trend than the presence of κ-carbides or ε-martensite

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements per material state
characterization_methods.purpose: measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and total elongation
characterization_methods.key_findings: yield strength and UTS increase while tensile elongation drops with Al content (2–11 wt.% Al)

characterization_methods.purpose: hardness screening of the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl RAP materials
characterization_methods.key_findings: hardness increases with Al content (per Fig. 6; the 550 °C/24 h curve is not separately shown in the provided text)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction by grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques
characterization_methods.purpose: microstructure investigation (check for cracks, pores, macrosegregations; recrystallization)
characterization_methods.key_findings: no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl alloy class, yield strength and ultimate tensile strength both increase while tensile elongation drops as Al content increases from 2 to 11 wt.% Al; XRD screening indicates increasing ferrite content is more relevant to this trend than κ-carbides or ε-martensite (block b0026).

The specific mechanical-property data plotted in Fig. 6 for the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl system correspond to the as-quenched, 400 °C/24 h, 500 °C/24 h, and 600 °C/24 h conditions; the 550 °C/24 h condition assigned to this sample is part of the RAP aging matrix (block b0020) but its individual numeric data points are not separately tabulated in the provided text.
Five Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl alloys were synthesized with Al varying in the 2–11 wt.% range, but the individual Al levels are not enumerated in the text (blocks b0019, b0020, b0026).
The RAP method screened two different sets of five Fe-Mn-C-based weight-reduced Al-containing compositions, each exposed to nine respective heat treatments, within 35 h (block b0021).
